## Summary

I changed the `customerCode` format from `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` to `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` with a per-city sequence.

**`AssignCustomerCode.java`** — the derivation logic:
- `CITY3` = upper-cased first three letters of `owner.getCity()`
- `LAST3` = upper-cased first three letters of the last name (unchanged)
- `NNNN` = per-city sequence: one more than the count of existing owners whose city matches (was previously a global count of all owners)

```java
String city3 = city.substring(0, Math.min(3, city.length())).toUpperCase();
String last3 = lastName.substring(0, Math.min(3, lastName.length())).toUpperCase();
int sequence = (int) ownerRepository.findAll().stream()
        .filter(existing -> city.equalsIgnoreCase(existing.getCity()))
        .count() + 1;
owner.setCustomerCode(String.format("%s-%s-%04d", city3, last3, sequence));
```

**`AssignMembershipNumber.java`** — the membership number is `customerCode + "-M" + YY`, so it's rebuilt on the new format automatically; I only updated its javadoc example (`SYD-SMI-0007-M26`).

Everything derived from the customerCode flows from these two steps, so the membership number now sits on the city-prefixed code without further changes. Full suite: 26/26 green.
